newsitem.title: USA: M.G. Products says must negotiate refinancing.
newsitem.headline: M.G. Products says must negotiate refinancing.

text.p: M.G. Products Inc said Wednesday it must negotiate the refinancing of a portion of its borrowings and may be liable for significant future rental payments for closed facilities.

The company, which makes residential lighting fixtures, made the disclosure as it reported a net loss of $7.5 million for the year ended December 31, 1996, or a loss of $0.65 a share, on revenues of $21.3 million. The net loss includes one-time restructuring charges of $1.7 million, it said.
For the full year 1995, M.G. reported a net loss of $7.4 million or a loss of $0.78 a share, on revenues of $28.3 milion.
The lower 1996 sales were because of a drop in the number of customers, which include major retailers, and a drop in placement of products with existing customers, it said.

It said that due to its continued losses and cash flow shortages, the opinion of its independent auditors attached to the audit report for 1996 will contain a note on the company's ability as a going concern.
It said that for during the fourth quarter of 1996, it closed its Tijuana, Mexico, production plant, resulting in a $1.6 million charge.

The closure was in addition to the elimination of its in-store service group and relocation of the Memphis, Tenn., distributoin center to San Antonio. It said these steps were taken to help bring back the company to profitability.
